text: Dawn. We paddled out at dawn.
Leash. My leash broke on the second wave.
Wax. I forgot the wax at home.
Rip. A rip took him past the rocks.
Shore. He swam back to the shore alone.
Borrow. I borrowed a board from a guy on the sand.
Give up. I didn't give up, but I wanted to.
Rescue. The lifeguard rescued two people that morning.

You look destroyed. What happened yesterday?
Long story. We paddled out at dawn. It was perfect for about ten minutes.
And then?
My leash broke on the second wave. The board went to the shore without me.
Please tell me you swam in straight away.
I tried. A rip took me past the rocks. I swam for ten minutes and I didn't move.
That is exactly when people panic. Did you give up?
No. I stopped fighting it and I swam sideways, like the coach said. Then a guy on a red board came out and helped me in.
A local rescued you and you still went back out. Of course you did.
What happened?
My leash broke and I lost my board.
Can I borrow a board?
I didn't fight the rip. I swam sideways.
Somebody helped me and I got back in.

Right, end of shift report. We had three rescues today. The first one was at seven in the morning, a swimmer near the rocks, and that one was easy. The second one was two surfers with one board between them, and honestly that was their own fault. The third one was at eleven. A rip took a young boy past the flags. He didn't panic, he waved, and we reached him in two minutes. Good kid. Nobody went to hospital today and after lunch everybody swam between the flags, so I call that a good day.

You will not believe my morning. I was paddling back out and I saw a boy in the rip with no board. So I turned around and I went straight to him. He was fine, actually. He didn't panic at all. He stopped fighting the current and he swam sideways, exactly like you are supposed to. We came in together and he just laughed. Then he asked me about the sandbank, so I lent him my old board and he went straight back out. Fifteen years old, maybe. Legend.
